premises: High oxygen-affinity elements (e.g., Cr, Al) preferentially segregate to the surface of HEAs at high temperature.
This surface segregation catalyzes the formation of a continuous, protective oxide scale.
The resulting oxide scale is slow-growing and acts as a diffusion barrier.
Conventional alloys with similar composition but lower complexity lack this segregation mechanism.
The mechanism is effective under high-temperature oxidative conditions (>700°C).
